title: Execution is one-shot and has no safe suspension or resume contract
expected_semantics: A debugger session should stop at a semantic event, expose a consistent state, and resume or terminate under an explicit stop condition.
actual_behavior_limitation: mncs execute accepts a complete request and emits a terminal JSON result; there is no session handle, safe point, stop-condition injection, or resumable state.
why_capability_matters: Without suspension, breakpoints/watchpoints/step cannot be implemented correctly by an external wrapper; re-execution changes the experiment and is not a stop.
current_workaround: Report these capabilities as unsupported and provide immutable post-execution inspection plus trace filtering.

host_language_code_required.why: The host can impose a process timeout but cannot safely suspend an MNCS semantic execution.

proposed_primitive_or_semantic_direction: Define explicit semantic safe points and a runtime debug session protocol with stop-condition binding, pause/inspect/resume state tokens, and ownership rules for effects.
alternatives_considered: kill/restart around a matching trace event
resolution_criteria: A runtime fixture can stop at a declared semantic event, inspect typed state, and resume with a documented effect/scheduler guarantee.
